answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens in an escrow haven. Multi-agent audit committees use topological cut verifications to inspect transaction subgraphs. If collusion is detected, auditing nodes reach a consensus summit to execute stake slashing, cracking fraudulent clusters open like a walnut shell. Splitting identities across topological cuts imposes a superlinear attacker cost that renders coordinated Sybil proliferation economically unviable.
